key_insight: MRI-derived kidney geometries coupled with FEM elastography yielded biomechanical features that distinguished CKD from healthy controls.
engineering_relevance: The framework links conventional kidney MRI to computational tissue mechanics, potentially enabling renal biomechanical assessment without dedicated MRE acquisition.
method: Convert kidney segmentation masks into watertight surfaces and tetrahedral FEM meshes.
Simulate harmonic waves using a nearly incompressible Kelvin–Voigt tissue model.
Estimate complex shear modulus via Helmholtz inversion and classify CKD using derived features.
evidence_signal: Estimated stiffness was consistent with published renal MRE ranges, and machine learning classification reached up to 86.26% cross-validation accuracy with an AUC of 0.92.
watch_item: Agreement with published stiffness ranges does not establish patient-specific accuracy; direct mechanical validation and independent clinical testing remain needed.
paper_title: Finite Element Elastographic Analysis of Kidney MRI for Computational Assessment of Chronic Kidney Disease
